process: What constitutes 'mutual agreement'? Contract requires mutual agreement on assignments; whose burden to document?
Are verbal variations enforceable? Contract requires written variations; does this bar all oral modifications?

Are 'Loss of Engagement' invoices valid? Contract is for completed work, not opportunity loss
Does Cameron have claim for damages? Depends on whether enforceable agreement existed
Was termination properly executed? One month notice appears to comply with contract terms

legal_prognosis: SOPE's position appears significantly stronger due to: (1) Written contract variation requirement; (2) Lack of written project agreements; (3) Communication breakdown documentation; (4) Proper termination notice execution; (5) Cameron's documentation and timing deficiencies. Absent compelling evidence of the verbal agreement and Cameron's responsiveness, SOPE's contractual protections likely defeat Cameron's claims.
conclusion: This dispute centers on enforceability of an alleged verbal 'win the work, do the work' agreement made in January 2025. Cameron claims this agreement entitled him to delivery assignments on projects where he contributed to presales work. SOPE denies the agreement and asserts that any such variation would require writing per the February 13, 2023 contract. SOPE's position appears significantly stronger, and likely outcome absent settlement favors SOPE.
